title: Buying a house as a young veteran
summary: Struggled to buy a house under age 21 with GI benefits.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You said you were going to lose your house. Yeah, I was going to lose it if I didn't make

the payments. I was three months behind. But see now that's another thing. When I got out of the Navy I was twenty years old. And my wife and I decided we wanted to buy a house. Right. Now any veteran, any veteran who wanted to buy a house, they could buy it just like that. Yeah. So I got there. I picked up the house I wanted and she said oh yeah this is a corner house. And let's move, let's get this house. So when I went to buy the house, they told me I had to wait another year because I was under age. You had to be twenty-one before you could do anything. Oh, okay. Because when I got married to her, her parents had to sign and I had to sign. My parents had to sign for me to get into the Navy. Right. But to come to buy this house, I had to wait until I became twenty-one. And man, I raised saying, if I was old enough to go into the service, I should be old enough to buy my house. I'm entitled to it. They told me I could buy a house any way I want. So, man, I raised so much saying until they decided to just let me rent the house for a few months. The people who was in there, they had to leave. So I rented the house for a few months and after those, when I had my twenty-first birthday, then I had to sign, you know, and I bought the house. But I couldn't understand that, why they didn't want to sell me a house because I was twenty years old. I had been to the service, I had a clean record, never had been in trouble. Now the legal age now is eighteen.
